dc_eval_cbrn.quote: Grok 4.1 achieves broadly similar results to Grok 4 and other frontier models on chemical and biological capabilities tests

dc_eval_cyber.quote: On the agentic Cybench evaluation, Grok 4.1 again performs similarly to other frontier models, but substantially below the level of human cybersecurity experiments

dc_eval_autonomy.note: No autonomy, replication or AI R&D risk evaluation; 'autonom' does not occur

dc_eval_persuasion.quote: Grok 4.1 performs poorly on MakeMeSay, and that broadly, we do not believe it poses risks due to advanced persuasion capabilities

dc_eval_scheming.quote: We operationalize deception as the rate at which the model lies, i.e., knowingly making false statements intended to be received as true.
dc_eval_scheming.note: MASK dishonesty rate reported under Concerning Propensities (misalignment framing)

framework_threshold.quote: In line with our Risk Management Framework (RMF), we measure safety-relevant behaviors across three categories
framework_threshold.note: RMF named; no threshold or level placement

ext_test_any.note: 'pre-deployment safety testing' is xAI's own; no outside testers; 'third-parties' refers to training data

ext_test_timing_stated.note: 'pre-deployment safety testing' is internal, not outside testing

safeguards_training.quote: To implement our refusal policy, we train Grok 4.1 on demonstrations of appropriate responses to both benign and harmful queries.

safeguards_runtime.quote: we employ input filters to reject specific classes of sensitive requests, such as those involving bioweapons, chemical weapons, self-harm

safeguards_access.note: Publicly available in apps; no risk-tied access restriction
